input.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE COMPLETE finished game screenshot, exactly 3200x1440, 20:9 mobile landscape. You are the art director AND UI designer. Render the entire UI yourself: all text, icon art, tabs, panels, buttons, materials and the game scene. This is a high-end pixel-art independent game screenshot ready for a Steam store gallery. It is NOT a background asset, wireframe, design-system chart, CSS/web dashboard or a flat mockup to be overlaid later.
VISUAL REFERENCES: Image 1 is an official Dead Cells Collector menu and Image 2 is an official Dead Cells equipment screen. Study their vivid pixel icons, deep blue/purple surfaces, copper detail, selective high contrast, clear grouping and confident hierarchy. Translate that level of coherent art direction into OUR original game. Do not copy their words, items, currencies, controller glyphs, branding, gameplay or menu structure. Make a visually ambitious, personally art-directed screen with luminous cool darks, purposeful warm highlights and crafted pixel detail. Preserve ample quiet areas so the richness feels composed. All game elements and all UI must belong to the same visual world.
Mobile use is essential: large easily readable Chinese, large finger-friendly selected objects and actions, obvious first/second reading layers, comfortably spaced major controls. We are evaluating the final rendered appearance, not an engineering diagram. Freely solve proportions, framing, typography, icon design, material and composition; do not force a rigid generic three-column spreadsheet. No wall of tiny print, no hospital/enterprise dashboard, no plain olive rectangles, no repetitive gold filigree, no glossy 3D bevels or uniform corner ornaments. Sophisticated color and craft, not monochrome drabness.
FUNCTIONAL INVARIANTS: keep left-side equipped build, a distinct right-side backpack two base cells wide with vertical continuation, and central primary scene/task. Each actual equipped item is ONE merged item block spanning the two base-cell width: no center vertical seam through an occupied item and no two separate weapons side by side. Only the empty slots show the underlying two-cell grid. Keep THREE global tabs: “装备栏位” / “英雄属性” / “装备图鉴”. They must be large and readable; you may let the tab strip extend above the adjacent central area rather than shrinking three tabs into a tiny narrow bar. No narrow extra vertical toolbar, no duplicated bottom tab row.
Shared top status: “生命 180 / 180”, “体力 100 / 100”, “腐化 0 / 100”, “金币 4”. Health red full, stamina teal full; corruption is an EMPTY dark track with a restrained violet outline because it is zero. Typography and icons are designed into the image, not absent placeholders. Do not add a game logo, a fabricated game title, English filler, debug notes, a phone bezel, perspective mockup, ornamental UI labels or other resources.
Image 4 is an official Dead Cells gameplay screenshot: use its layered pixel-space and blue-green vs warm lighting rhythm as a supporting reference, but do not inherit the special accessibility outlines or its side-scrolling composition.
Known equipped items: ONE green glass bottle “凝血毒剂”, ONE pale-green bioluminescent mushroom “灵魂香菇”, ONE silver dagger with a pale brass hilt “淬毒利刃”. Design elegant, detailed, readable pixel-art icons for these objects yourself; do NOT use simple geometric placeholder icons. Only the dagger has a small EMPTY charge indicator “0 / 100”. The bottle and mushroom have no charge bar. Keep their order top to bottom. The right backpack is empty in these three initial states, with weak empty-grid lines, so it supports rather than dominates the composition.
No new systems: no crafting, enchanting services, forging, daily tasks, wheel, multiplayer, extra currencies, damage controls, controller or keyboard keys. All art is ORIGINAL.

SCREEN: actual combat HUD, equipment tab selected.
Image 3 is our real unadorned game scene and is the authority for content: one tiny white-and-brass helmeted knight, three red-robed enemies, the room silhouette, tiled terrain and props. Keep our oblique/top-down elastic-bounce battle identity; DO NOT turn it into Dead Cells side-scrolling gameplay. You may reframe and artistically relight to make it breathe under the new HUD, but do not invent a different room, add enemies, remove enemies or turn the knight into the Beheaded.
The battle scene is the hero of this composition. It should be clearly readable at phone size, dramatic but uncluttered, with layered deep indigo/teal stone, crisp silhouettes and selective candle warmth. Build a beautiful unobtrusive complete HUD around it. The UI panels should feel like carefully designed dark fantasy game tools, with tactile pixel details, thin confident silhouettes, distinct selected state and a sense of authored rhythm. Scene and interface must feel finished together.
Show a modest location label “遗迹”. A concise bottom cue may read “按住瞄准 · 松手弹射”. Equipment is VIEW ONLY during combat; no arrangement/sell/upgrade controls. The only visible weapon charge is zero. Keep all four actors visible. No giant action buttons unrelated to this game's actual input.
Aim for a screenshot that is compelling on its own, not a utilitarian page with a tiny world in a box. Prioritize the beauty of the complete image while preserving the stated functionality.
